newsitem.title: USA: EMERGING DEBT MODESTLY HIGHER AFTER U.S. AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: EMERGING DEBT MODESTLY HIGHER AFTER U.S. AUCTION.

text.p: Emerging market debt followed U.S. Treasuries higher in very thin trading on Wednesday, traders said.
Investors had been sidelined ahead of the U.S. 10-year note auction, they said. But activity remained sparse even after the sale results were posted.
"It's very slow," one Brady bond trader said. "The auction didn't help us out much."
The U.S. Treasury placed $12 billion of 10-year notes at 6.205 percent. The yield was in line with market expectations, but demand was thinner than expected, market players said.
Fueled by apparent progress on its London Club restructuring, Russian issues outperformed the rest of the emerging debt market on Wednesday.
Vnesh loans and IAN bonds surged in overnight trading, and the rally continued during the U.S. session, traders said.
"Russia's doing really well," one Brady trader said.
"We saw two or three different buyers today," he added, describing the clients as dedicated country funds and hedge funds.
Dollar-denominated Russian Vnesh were up 7/8 at 98-7/8.
Elsewhere, benchmark Brazil "C" bonds rose 3/8 to 83-3/4, tightening about five basis points to comparable Treasuries.
On Tuesday, Brazil posted a much larger-than-expected trade deficit of $811 million for June. The news affected the country's debt little, however, analysts said.

"The number was a little bit of a surprise, but it looks to be somewhat of an aberration with a lot of oil imports enterring the country on the last day of the month," said Peter Greenbaum, a Latin America economist at Smith Barney.
Other major Latin issues also rose modestly. Argentina FRBs rose 1/8 to 95-5/8 and Mexico Pars were up 1/2 at 82.
U.S. Treasuries recorded slight gains on the day. The bellwhether 30-year T-bond climbed 4/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
